abstract.text: The vacuum expectation values of conserved currents play an essential role in the generalized hydrodynamics of integrable quantum field theories. We use analytic continuation to extend these results for the excited state expectation values in a finite volume. Our formulas are valid for diagonally scattering theories and incorporate all finite size corrections.

thesis.text: Analytic continuation of the generalized-hydrodynamics/TBA pairing yields exact finite-volume excited-state expectation values of conserved charges and currents for diagonally scattering integrable theories, including all finite-size corrections.

identity.title: Exact finite volume expectation values of conserved currents

question.text: How can one extend the vacuum expectation values of conserved currents in generalized hydrodynamics to exact finite-volume excited-state expectation values for diagonally scattering integrable quantum field theories, including all finite-size corrections?

sections.summary: Motivates the problem from statistical physics and AdS/CFT, reviews GHD conservation laws, TBA occupation numbers, dressed charge/current densities, Leclair-Mussardo form factors, and the mirror-channel finite-volume vacuum expectations that the paper will generalize.
sections.title: Vacuum expectation values in generalized hydrodynamics

sections.summary: Introduces excited-state TBA by analytically continuing the volume/temperature and picking up pole residues; encodes the resulting discrete contributions in a new convolution/pairing, then conjectures the same charge and current formulas with this pairing.
sections.title: Excited-state analytic continuation and modified pairing

sections.summary: Separates discrete physical-particle contributions from continuous quasiparticle dressing using the quantization condition, derives the Gaudin matrix and its inverse, and rewrites current and charge expectations in terms of the old dressing, showing the leading term matches [8,9].
sections.title: Physical-particle separation and Gaudin matrix

sections.summary: Applies β_i=Lδ_i1 to obtain finite-volume excited-state diagonal matrix elements. Charges become simple eigenvalues; currents require Gaudin dressing but reduce to the known asymptotic formula when vacuum polarization is neglected. Checks against excited LM form factors and concludes.
sections.title: Finite-volume formulas, checks, and conclusion
